best-broadway-shows.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows: March 2026

Broadway enters spring 2026 with a remarkably diverse lineup that balances groundbreaking revivals with inventive new works. This month's top ten shows average an impressive 83 out of 100 from critics, reflecting the exceptional quality currently on display across Manhattan's theater district.

Leading the pack, **Hamilton** continues its unprecedented run as critics' top choice, with its revolutionary hip-hop retelling of American history still captivating audiences more than a decade after its debut. The show's 90/100 rating from 43 reviews confirms its status as a modern masterpiece that has fundamentally changed what Broadway musicals can be.

Close behind, **Maybe Happy Ending** emerges as one of the season's most delightful surprises—a tender robot love story that critics describe as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years. Meanwhile, **The Book of Mormon** maintains its position as a comedic powerhouse, proving that irreverent satire continues to resonate with both critics and audiences.

The current landscape showcases Broadway's remarkable range: Cole Escola's absurdist **Oh, Mary!** brings riotous comedy to Mary Todd Lincoln's story, while the timely **Ragtime** revival addresses America's historical tensions with renewed urgency. Visual spectacles like **The Lion King** and **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** demonstrate that theatrical magic remains as potent as ever, and **Buena Vista Social Club** transports audiences to Cuba through intoxicating music and choreography.

Whether you're drawn to hip-hop history lessons, robot romance, or spectacular stagecraft, March 2026 offers something exceptional for every theatrical taste. Explore the full rankings below to find your next unforgettable Broadway experience.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves deeper into the spring season, the play lineup presents an eclectic mix ranging from absurdist comedy to psychological thriller, with an average critic score of 74/100 across our featured productions.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's audacious reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, cocktail-swilling narcissist. The absurdist farce earns an impressive 83/100 from critics who praise its riotous humor and bold irreverence toward historical drama. Close behind, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** continues to captivate audiences with its technical wizardry, scoring 82/100. While critics note the story's unevenness, the production's spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions remain undeniable draws for theater fans.

**Bug** marks a notable entry this month as Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller finally makes its Broadway debut. The production scores 74/100, with reviewers responding positively to this intense two-hander's arrival on the Great White Way. Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** delivers impressive special effects and technical achievements, though its three-hour runtime and overstuffed prequel narrative leave some critics wanting tighter storytelling.

This month's selection demonstrates Broadway's range—from historical satire to fantasy spectacle to intimate psychological drama. The strongest productions succeed by either delivering exceptional performances and writing (as with *Oh, Mary!*) or compensating for narrative weaknesses with stunning technical execution (as with *Harry Potter*).

Whether you're drawn to cutting-edge comedy, magical stagecraft, or psychological intensity, March offers distinct theatrical experiences across the spectrum.

best-broadway-shows-for-kids.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows for Kids

**March 2026** — Broadway offers a robust selection of family-friendly productions this month, with six shows delivering the spectacle, music, and storytelling that captivate young audiences. These productions average a solid 74/100 critic score, representing some of the most technically ambitious and visually impressive work currently on stage.

**The Lion King** continues to set the standard for family theater nearly three decades after its premiere, earning the highest critic score at 83/100. Julie Taymor's revolutionary puppetry and costume design remain unmatched in their ability to transport audiences to the African savanna, making this Disney adaptation a perennial must-see for families visiting New York.

**Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** follows closely at 82/100, offering older children and teens an immersive journey into J.K. Rowling's wizarding world. While critics note the story doesn't always match the original novels' narrative strength, the production's magical stagecraft and technical illusions consistently draw praise as some of Broadway's most sophisticated.

The remaining shows—**Aladdin**, **& Juliet**, **Wicked**, and **MJ The Musical**—each bring distinct appeals, from classic Disney storytelling to jukebox musical energy to biographical spectacle. Parents should note that age-appropriateness varies considerably across these productions, with some featuring more complex themes or longer runtimes that may challenge younger children.

Broadway's family offerings this March balance artistic ambition with accessibility, though the critical consensus suggests that technical spectacle often outpaces narrative innovation in this category. Families planning their theater outings should consider both critic assessments and their children's specific interests when selecting from these six productions.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted. These productions launched during an unprecedented year that would soon see the complete shutdown of live performance, making their brief initial runs all the more poignant in retrospect.

Among the five notable productions from that tumultuous year, **A Soldier's Play** stands as the clear critical favorite. Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama, which waited decades for its Broadway debut, earns the strongest reviews for its powerful examination of race and justice within the military, brought to life through what critics describe as stellar performances.

Close behind, **Les Misérables** returns in a grittier reimagining at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This rebooted production divides some traditionalists but largely wins praise for its fresh approach to the beloved musical, proving that even established classics can find new resonance through bold reinterpretation.

The remaining productions showcase Broadway's range: **My Name is Lucy Barton** features Laura Linney in a solo performance that critics universally admire, even as they debate the adaptation itself; **Grand Horizons** offers boulevard comedy elevated by Broadway veterans Jane Alexander and James Cromwell; and Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** takes the most polarizing approach, with its radical staging earning both enthusiastic champions and skeptical detractors.

With an average critical score of 73/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season demonstrates both artistic ambition and the enduring power of established works finding new life. Whether you're drawn to thought-provoking drama or bold reimaginings of classics, these productions offer compelling reasons to explore what made this brief theatrical moment memorable.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:

These productions, which debuted during Broadway's emotional reopening, continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike, earning an impressive average score of 81/100.

The standout among these ten productions is **Dana H.**, a groundbreaking docudrama that pushes theatrical boundaries through Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary lip-sync performance. This unconventional work earns the highest critical acclaim at 86/100, mesmerizing audiences with its innovative approach to storytelling. Close behind is **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**, Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that completely transforms the August Wilson Theatre into the titular nightclub, creating an experience that critics widely celebrate as both stunning and essential.

The list also features enduring classics alongside bold new voices. **The Phantom of the Opera**, still captivating audiences with Andrew Lloyd Webber's infectious melodies, shares space with urgent contemporary works like **Pass Over**, which marked Broadway's historic reopening, and **Is This a Room**, a verbatim thriller drawn from FBI transcripts. Musical theater is well-represented through Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** revival and the pop-infused phenomenon **SIX**, while intimate character studies like **Lackawanna Blues** and **Clyde's** showcase the power of American storytelling.

Whether you're drawn to experimental theater, classic spectacle, or contemporary drama, these productions from 2021's pivotal season offer something for every theatergoer to discover.

best-broadway-shows-2022.intro:

Leading the field is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics have embraced as a near-perfect achievement, deftly balancing sharp comedy with genuine emotional depth. Close behind, both **Into the Woods** and **A Strange Loop** demonstrate the breadth of 2022's offerings—the former a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as fitting tribute to the late composer, the latter a brazenly original meta-musical that pushes theatrical boundaries.

What distinguishes this collection is its remarkable diversity of voices and forms. For theatergoers looking to understand this pivotal season, these ten productions offer an essential cross-section of contemporary American theater at its finest.

best-broadway-shows-2023.intro:

The year's theatrical landscape showcases remarkable diversity—from intimate solo performances to technically ambitious spectacles. Leading the pack is Maria Friedman's revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which finally realizes the potential of Sondheim's once-maligned musical with emotionally resonant performances that have won over critics and audiences alike. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** demonstrates that commercial properties can yield serious theatrical artistry, with its technically stunning production earning praise for transcending mere fan service.

The year also proves particularly strong for revivals with contemporary urgency. **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama featuring Sarah Paulson, earns recognition as a modern masterpiece, while **Purlie Victorious** finds new relevance in Ossie Davis's 1961 satire. **Parade**, starring Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond, similarly resonates with timely themes that speak to current audiences.

New works make their mark as well, from Alex Edelman's brilliant solo show **Just for Us** to the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham**, which reimagines Hamlet at a Black family barbecue. **Stereophonic**, despite initially modest critical scores, has emerged as a word-of-mouth phenomenon, with audiences embracing its immersive three-hour journey into a 1970s recording studio.

Whether you're seeking classical revivals, bold new voices, or innovative adaptations, 2023's Broadway offerings continue to reward theatergoers with performances that justify the journey to New York.

# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway enters March 2026, we look back at the plays that premiered in 2020, a pivotal year that saw promising productions launch just before the industry faced unprecedented challenges. The five plays featured here represent the range of theatrical ambition on display during that brief window, from classic revivals to intimate new works.

Leading our rankings is **A Soldier's Play**, Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally receives its long-awaited Broadway debut. Critics consistently praise this revival for its powerful examination of race, justice, and military life, with the production earning strong notices across the board (78/100 from 29 reviews). The show demonstrates how classic American plays can resonate with renewed urgency when given thoughtful, well-executed productions.

Also making waves is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This grittier reboot earns largely positive reviews (77/100), though the radical approach to the beloved musical doesn't win over all critics. Meanwhile, **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases Laura Linney in a solo performance that divides reviewers—her work garners universal acclaim even as opinions split on the adaptation itself.

Rounding out the list are **Grand Horizons**, a boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, and Ivo van Hove's provocative **West Side Story**, which reimagines the classic with video design and unconventional staging choices that prove polarizing.

With an average critical score of 73/100 across these five productions, March 2020's plays offer diverse theatrical experiences worth exploring. Browse our detailed reviews below to find the production that best matches your interests.

# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway productions that premiered in 2021 represent a remarkable moment of theatrical rebirth. Following the industry's pandemic shutdown, these shows didn't just reopen theaters—they redefined what Broadway could be.

The class of 2021 showcases exceptional range, from intimate experimental works to lavish spectacles. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance that critics consistently describe as mesmerizing and unforgettable. Close behind, Rebecca Frecknall's **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** earns widespread acclaim for its immersive reimagining that completely transforms the August Wilson Theatre into a pre-war Berlin nightclub. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** stands as an epic theatrical triumph, with critics praising its extraordinary ensemble performances and stunning direction across three acts spanning 164 years.

The year also brought vital revivals like Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** and powerful new voices including Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over**, which appropriately served as Broadway's post-shutdown reopening production. Verbatim theater makes a compelling case with **Is This a Room**, while solo performances shine in **Lackawanna Blues**. Even **The Phantom of the Opera**, still running from its 1988 premiere, receives fresh critical attention during this period.

With an impressive average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 Broadway season demonstrates both artistic ambition and commercial appeal. Whether you're drawn to experimental formats, reimagined classics, or spectacular productions, these shows offer essential viewing for any serious theater enthusiast.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a watershed moment for American theater—a year when the industry roared back from pandemic closures with remarkable artistic ambition and diversity of voices.

The season's crown jewel is undoubtedly **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition. With a stellar 88/100 critical score, it represents the rare show that achieves both emotional depth and pitch-perfect comedy. Close behind are two equally impressive productions: **Into the Woods**, Ennio Flaiano's stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as both tribute and revelation, and **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer-winning meta-musical that pushes boundaries with its brazenly original voice.

What's particularly striking about this collection of ten shows is their collective excellence—an average score of 83/100—and their thematic breadth. The lineup spans from Suzan-Lori Parks' electrifying **Topdog/Underdog** revival to Tom Stoppard's haunting Holocaust meditation **Leopoldstadt**, from Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo storytelling to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire **Ain't No Mo'**.

Notably, four Pulitzer Prize-winning plays appear on this list (**A Strange Loop**, **Between Riverside and Crazy**, **How I Learned to Drive**, and **Cost of Living**), underscoring the season's commitment to challenging, substantive drama. These productions tackle complex themes—identity, trauma, caregiving, systemic injustice—with unflinching honesty.

Whether you're catching final performances or discovering these shows through cast recordings and published scripts, the 2022 season offers a masterclass in contemporary American theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2023 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, with an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across our top ten selections.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which scores 85/100 and stands as a remarkable vindication of Sondheim's once-maligned work. The production earns praise for its emotional resonance and fresh interpretation, proving that great material sometimes simply needs the right moment and approach. Tied at the top is **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, the West End transfer that surprises critics by transcending its source material with technically stunning stagecraft that works as compelling theatre in its own right.

The year also showcases vital American voices and stories. **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama featuring Sarah Paulson, earns widespread acclaim as a modern masterpiece, while **Purlie Victorious** receives a long-overdue revival that proves Ossie Davis's 1961 satire remains bracingly relevant. Meanwhile, **Parade** resonates with urgent contemporary significance, and **Fat Ham** brings Pulitzer-winning innovation to the Hamlet framework.

From solo performances like **Just for Us** to immersive experiences like **Stereophonic**, and from the vocal power of **Sweeney Todd** to the infectious rhythms of **Buena Vista Social Club**, these productions represent the breadth and vitality of straight plays and play-with-music productions on Broadway. Whether you're drawn to intimate storytelling, ambitious revivals, or technically dazzling spectacle, these critically acclaimed shows offer compelling reasons to experience theatre at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves into spring 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—ranging from intimate character studies to ambitious historical musicals—maintains an impressive average critic score of 83/100, reflecting a particularly strong theatrical season.

**Stereophonic** leads the field with a score of 89/100, with critics celebrating David Adjmi's behind-the-scenes look at a 1970s rock band as an authentic exploration of the creative process and artistic collaboration. The production's theatrical craftsmanship has resonated deeply with reviewers who praise its ability to capture both the mundane and transcendent aspects of making music.

**Operation Mincemeat** follows closely at 88/100, earning acclaim as an inventive, high-energy ensemble piece that made the successful leap from grassroots sensation to West End transfer. Meanwhile, **Cole Escola's Oh, Mary!** has emerged as the season's comedic standout, presenting an absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist that critics describe as a riotous tour de force.

The list also features notable revivals, including Audra McDonald's deeply personal interpretation of Mama Rose in **Gypsy** and a lavish new staging of **Oliver!**, alongside original works like **Maybe Happy Ending**, a robot love story that critics hail as one of Broadway's most emotionally resonant musicals in recent memory.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new voices, classic revivals reimagined, or genre-defying theatrical experiments, these critically acclaimed productions offer a comprehensive view of what's currently thriving on Broadway.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the plays that opened last year continue to demonstrate remarkable range and vitality, from intimate character studies to ambitious historical epics.

The season's highest-rated offering is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down **All My Sons**, which earns widespread critical acclaim for transforming Arthur Miller's classic into a visceral emotional experience. Van Hove's minimalist approach allows the ensemble cast to deliver performances of exceptional intensity, proving that bold directorial vision can breathe new life into canonical American drama. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences and critics alike why this quirky musical comedy endures, with reviewers praising both its airtight construction and surprising emotional depth.

The season showcases significant diversity in subject matter and style. **Paddington The Musical** brings technical wizardry to family entertainment with its remarkably lifelike puppet work, while **Liberation** tackles feminist themes through Wohl's ambitious memory play structure. Historical narratives receive fresh treatment in the timely **Ragtime** revival, anchored by Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance, and the darkly comic **Dead Outlaw**, which transforms outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre posthumous journey into rock-inflected musical theater.

Pulitzer winner **English** continues to earn praise for Sanaz Toossi's nuanced exploration of language and identity, while classic comedy thrives in the West End transfer of **The Producers**. With an average critic score of 85/100 across these ten productions, the 2025 Broadway season demonstrates both artistic ambition and critical success.

Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, innovative new work, or spectacular family entertainment, these plays offer compelling reasons to experience live theater this spring.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a lean but noteworthy moment for new Broadway plays, with Tracy Letts' psychological thriller making its long-awaited debut on the Great White Way.

**Bug** leads this month's offerings, earning largely positive notices in its first Broadway production. Originally premiered in 1996, Letts' paranoid two-hander about a drifter and a motel dweller descending into shared delusion finally reaches Broadway nearly three decades after its initial run. Critics award the production a solid 74/100 across 35 reviews, with particular praise directed toward its central performances and the claustrophobic intensity that has made the play a favorite in regional theaters for years.

The relatively quiet March landscape for new play openings reflects Broadway's typical seasonal rhythms, with producers often holding major productions for the spring Tony Awards eligibility window or waiting until after the ceremony to launch summer and fall programming. This measured pace allows theatergoers to focus their attention on individual productions rather than navigating an oversaturated market.

While the 2026 Broadway season has opened modestly in terms of new play volume, the quality of what has arrived suggests careful curation rather than scarcity. **Bug**'s reception demonstrates that well-executed productions of established dramatic works can still command critical attention and audience interest, even decades after their original premieres.

For theater enthusiasts planning their Broadway calendar, this focused selection makes March an ideal time to catch a psychologically intense drama before the spring season accelerates into its busier final stretch.
